name: অমৃতঘটেশ্বরর (কোড়ি কুড়গর) মন্দির, কোড়িক্করৈ
deity: অমৃতঘটেশ্বরর (কোড়ি কুড়গর, একটি স্বয়ম্ভু লিঙ্গ) রূপে শিব, দেবী অঞ্জনাক্ষী (মৈ তড়ঙ্গন্নি)-র সঙ্গে
period: তেবারম যুগ (৭ম শতাব্দীতে গীত); পরবর্তী চোল কাঠামোগত মন্দির
summary: কোড়িক্করৈতে — পয়েন্ট ক্যালিমেরে, যেখানে কাবেরী দেশ ভূমির দক্ষিণতম প্রান্তে সমুদ্রের সঙ্গে মেলে — শিব অমৃতঘটেশ্বরর রূপে সম্মানিত, কোড়ি কুড়গর, এক স্বয়ম্ভু লিঙ্গে পূজিত, দেবী অঞ্জনাক্ষীর সঙ্গে। সম্বন্দর ও সুন্দরর কর্তৃক গীত একটি পাডল পেট্র স্থলম্, এটি অমৃতম, মন্থিত সমুদ্রের সুধার সমুদ্রতীরবর্তী মন্দির।

sections.history: Kodikkarai — Point Calimere, the southern tip of the Kaveri delta where land meets sea — holds a Paadal Petra Sthalam, the Kodi Kuzhagar temple, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar and Sundarar. Believed first built by the Cholas, it carries several inscriptions of the Chola period. It stands in Nagapattinam district, by the Point Calimere wildlife sanctuary.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian seaside temple, the shrine enshrines Amirthagateswarar — the Kodi Kuzhagar — worshipped in a swayambhu, self-manifest lingam, with the goddess Anjanakshi (Mai Thadanganni) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The Navagrahas here are set in a straight line rather than the usual grid. Because of its remote coastal setting, the temple opens only about an hour each morning and evening.
sections.legends: The sthala legend tells of the churning of the milky ocean: the amritam, the nectar, was being borne in a pot (kudam) by Vayu, the wind, when the asuras raised a storm; a little of the nectar spilled here and took the form of a lingam. From that pot of nectar the lord is Amirthagateswarar — amrita-ghata, 'the nectar-pot lord' — and in Tamil Kodi Kuzhagar, the fair one of the land's end. The goddess Anjanakshi stands beside him.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a remote coastal shrine. Pilgrims on the Vedaranyam–Kodikkarai stretch of the Paadal Petra trail reach Point Calimere at the land's southern end.
sections.experience: At Kodikkarai the pilgrim comes to the land's end, where the delta runs out into the sea. Before Amirthagateswarar and Anjanakshi — the nectar-pot lord of the churned ocean — with the sanctuary's birds and the salt wind near, the visitor finds, in the hour the doors stand open, the far, unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple at the southern tip of the Tamil country.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Kodikkarai (Point Calimere) is the land's southern tip, about 11 km beyond Vedaranyam, in Nagapattinam district, by the Point Calimere wildlife sanctuary. Vedaranyam is the nearest town, with buses and taxis to the point; Nagapattinam and Tiruvarur are the nearest rail heads. The temple opens only about an hour each morning and evening.
